$comment: Known-answer vector for the rootfs digest (ADR-0047 §3; beads ley-line-open-39309e, ley-line-open-4f08ea). The rootfs digest is BLAKE3-256 (σ_bytes) over the exact bytes of rootfs.manifest.json, which is also the rootfs directory's name beneath the CAS root and RunReceipt.inputRoots[0]. `manifest` holds those bytes as a JSON string (UTF-8, no trailing newline). Both cases are the checked-in fixture tests/fixtures/oci-multilayer (linux/arm64). VERSION 2, which `leyline rootfs import-oci` writes: one compact JSON object with no whitespace, keys in the order version, entries; `version` 2; `entries` lists every directory except the root, every regular file and every symbolic link, in component-wise byte order of their paths (a directory before its entries, its entries before its next sibling), each entry's parent the root or a listed directory, no path twice; a directory is {type:"dir", path, mode}, mode within 0o1777 with 0o700 set (the importer clears setuid and setgid, keeps sticky, and sets owner rwx); a file is {type:"file", path, mode, blake3}, mode within 0o777 with 0o400 set, blake3 the content's lowercase hex BLAKE3-256; a link is {type:"symlink", path, target}, target 1 to 4096 bytes without NUL, never followed at import; the root directory is 0o755 and has no entry; strings escaped as serde_json escapes them. A reader accepts only these canonical bytes for a v2 tree, so one tree has one digest. VERSION 1, frozen and still read: keys version, files; files only (path, mode, blake3), directories implied at 0o755, no links; read in any byte form it shipped in. The v1 case is the same fixture imported before v2, its links resolved to copies. Consumed by leyline-runtime tests/oci_rootfs.rs (the_rootfs_manifest_vector_is_what_the_importer_writes), which checks that the importer writes exactly the v2 bytes for the fixture. A changed value is an identity migration, never an edit.
construction: blake3-256 over the exact bytes of rootfs.manifest.json
